defects.what: top slab reads far thicker than the 0.015 m spec in the front and side orthographic views — it occupies roughly 12-15% of total desk height as a solid band, i.e. ~0.09-0.11 m, about 6-7x the specified thickness. This is the single biggest silhouette deviation from the photo, where the top reads as a hairline compared to the panel height.
defects.measured: ~0.10 m rendered vs 0.015 m specified (front/side views)
defects.fix: Force top-slab dimensions.h to 0.015 m in the actual build geometry; check that no edge bevel, shadow-seam mesh, or material layering is inflating the apparent box height, since the three-quarter render shows a correctly thin slab but the ortho views do not.

summary: Overall macro silhouette (inverted-U of three glass planes, no apron/legs) and component count are on-target and match the mustMatch structural facts reasonably well in the three-quarter render. However the front/side orthographic views show a top slab that is dramatically thicker than the specified 0.015 m, which is a mustMatch violation on 'uniform 0.015 m glass thickness' and materially changes the proportion read of the desk from a thin floating glass top to a chunky tabletop. This needs a geometry fix before moving to the structural pass. Materials being flat is correct for this pass and not penalized; bracket/pad micro-detail is rightly absent at this stage.
